title: shmap-rs 1.4.0: a Rust port of shmap, with a reproducible cross-architecture benchmark suite
description:
A Rust port of shmap, a sketch-based long-read mapper that locates a read by k-mer set overlap rather than by alignment. Mapping decisions match the C++ original; the port is faster single-threaded, uses substantially less memory, and adds threading.

This release also archives the evidence. Every published figure is generated from a committed result set and verified against it, on two architectures:

  • x86_64 (Intel Xeon Gold 5218, 4 NUMA nodes) and aarch64 (ARM Neoverse-N1, 1 NUMA node), measured at the same commit with the same compiler and byte-identical inputs.
  • Every algorithmic counter — reads mapped, mapq-60 calls, buckets seeded, refined and reported — is identical across the two architectures, and all fifteen Winnowmap2 concordance figures reproduce to four decimal places.
  • Thread scaling on one NUMA node reaches 11.7x at 64 threads against 6.0x at 16 on four, which is the cross-socket memory-traffic ceiling shown against hardware rather than argued.
  • Run-to-run noise is measured rather than assumed, and the regression gate is calibrated to it per host.

New in 1.4.0: --per-read-stats emits one row per read so per-read cost can be plotted against the match count the seed heuristic exists to bound. Mapping output is unchanged.
